obligation: Owner report of a suspected CJI incident to the sheriff's LASO
citation: N92-R02: CJISSECPOL v6.1 IR-6 a. and b. (binding through the CJIS Security Addendum sec. 3.01; 28 CFR 20.33(a)(7)); POL-01 10.2
trigger: Any suspected incident on a device or account the owner uses to reach the sheriff's virtual desktop, including ransomware on the laptop, a lost hardware token, or CJI found outside the virtual desktop
deadline: Immediately, and no more than 1 hour after discovery
notify: Sheriff's local agency security officer (LASO), who routes it to the sheriff's incident handlers, the CJIS Systems Officer, and the FBI CJIS ISO (IR-6 b.)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - the laptop is the owner's only device for the sheriff's virtual desktop, so ransomware on it is a suspected CJI incident even if no CJI is stored there

obligation: Sheriff's report of a security violation to the CSO and the FBI (agency duty the owner supports)
citation: N92-R02: CJISSECPOL v6.1 Appendix H, Security Addendum sec. 4.01-4.03
trigger: Security violation involving a contractor with CJI access
deadline: The Addendum sets no deadline; it follows the state CJIS Systems Agency's procedure
notify: The sheriff reports to the CSO and the Director, FBI, with the actions taken by the sheriff and the owner. The FBI may suspend access
applies_at_this_tier: Sheriff's duty. The owner gives the LASO its actions and evidence on request

obligation: Owner notice to the county of a security incident
trigger: Security incident that may involve county data or the owner's county accounts (single sign-on, secure file transfer)
deadline: Within 24 hours of discovery. Owner target: within 4 hours, so the county can meet its own 12-hour ransomware clock if it applies
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - county extracts were on the laptop

obligation: Owner notice to the city of a security incident
citation: Contract CL-02 (confidentiality clause: prompt notice); POL-01 10.2
trigger: Unauthorized disclosure or incident that may involve city data or the owner's 311 accounts
deadline: Promptly (no hours stated). Owner rule: the same business day, and within 4 hours for ransomware
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - city exports were on the laptop

obligation: Florida county and municipality ransomware report (agency duty)
citation: Fla. Stat. 282.3185(5)(a)-(b); ransomware incident as defined in Fla. Stat. 282.0041
trigger: Ransomware incident that encrypts or renders unavailable a county's or municipality's data and is followed by a ransom demand
deadline: No later than 12 hours after discovery of the ransomware incident (48 hours for other incidents of severity level 3, 4, or 5)
notify: Cybersecurity Operations Center, the FDLE Cybercrime Office, and the sheriff with jurisdiction over the local government
applies_at_this_tier: County and city duty. Each decides with counsel whether county or city data encrypted or taken from the owner's laptop makes this their ransomware incident. The owner supplies the report content: summary of facts, date and location of the most recent backup and whether it was affected or cloud-based, types of data, estimated fiscal impact, and the ransom demand

obligation: Local government after-action report (agency duty)
trigger: Remediation of a cybersecurity or ransomware incident at a county or municipality
deadline: Within 1 week after remediation
applies_at_this_tier: County and city duty if they treated it as their incident. The owner provides the incident summary, resolution, and lessons in time

obligation: Ransom payment prohibition for county and city clients
trigger: Ransom demand affecting a county's or municipality's data
deadline: Applies at all times: a county or municipality may not pay or otherwise comply with a ransom demand
notify: Not a notice. Shapes the ransom decision (POL-01 10.4)
applies_at_this_tier: Binds the county and city clients. The owner will not pay over agency data without every affected agency's agreement

obligation: Third-party agent breach notice to the county or city
trigger: Breach of security (unauthorized access of data in electronic form containing personal information, 501.171(1)(a)) in a system the owner maintains for the county or city
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable, but no later than 10 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe it occurred. The owner gives the agency all information it needs for its own notices
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - applies directly to the owner as a third-party agent (501.171(1)(h)). County extracts include names with driver license numbers for about 2,100 people

obligation: Notice to Florida individuals (agency duty)
trigger: Breach of personal information of Florida residents
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe it occurred, unless a law enforcement delay (501.171(4)(b)) or a documented no-harm determination (501.171(4)(c)) applies
notify: Each affected Florida resident, by mail or email
applies_at_this_tier: County or city duty, decided with its counsel. The owner may send notices on the agency's behalf if asked (501.171(6)(b))

obligation: Notice to the Florida Department of Legal Affairs (agency duty)
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe it occurred (15 more days for notice to individuals only, if good cause is given in writing within 30 days)
applies_at_this_tier: Likely for the county if its extracts were taken (about 2,100 people with driver license numbers). The owner supplies counts

obligation: Notice to consumer reporting agencies (agency duty)
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at one time
deadline: Without unreasonable delay
applies_at_this_tier: Likely for the county if more than 1,000 residents are notified

obligation: Other states' breach laws
trigger: Affected individuals who live outside Florida (for example property owners who live elsewhere)
deadline: Varies by state
notify: Residents and regulators under each state's law
applies_at_this_tier: Agency duty in each state where affected individuals reside; the owner supplies residence data from the extracts

obligation: Supply chain incident coordination
citation: SP 800-53 IR-6(3) (Moderate baseline); CJISSECPOL v6.1 IR-6(3)
trigger: Incident involving a SaaS account the owner uses (productivity suite, password manager)
deadline: No deadline set; as soon as practicable
notify: The provider's security or abuse contact
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contract CL-01 (SP 800-53 Moderate)

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: Any ransom payment is considered
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if a sanctioned party is involved); FBI or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - all U.S. persons. Strict liability for payments to sanctioned parties

obligation: Law enforcement report (voluntary)
citation: OFAC advisory (Sept. 21, 2021) mitigating factor; owner practice
trigger: Ransomware or data theft confirmed
deadline: Owner target: within 48 hours, coordinated with the agencies
applies_at_this_tier: Voluntary. Coordinate with the county and city, which report to FDLE under Florida law

obligation: Cyber insurance claim notice
citation: Cyber endorsement on the professional liability policy (contract)
trigger: Suspected security incident
deadline: Per policy; call the breach hotline before hiring any response vendor
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual, not legal ($100,000 sublimit)

obligation: FTI unauthorized disclosure or data breach
citation: N92-R01: IRS Pub. 1075 sec. 1.8.4 (and TIGTA reporting)
trigger: Possible improper inspection or disclosure of federal tax information
deadline: Immediately, no later than 24 hours after discovery, without waiting for an internal investigation
notify: TIGTA and the IRS Office of Safeguards
applies_at_this_tier: No - the owner holds no FTI (the March 2026 FTI subcontract was declined)

obligation: HIPAA breach of unsecured PHI
trigger: Breach of unsecured PHI
deadline: Not applicable
applies_at_this_tier: No - the owner is not a business associate and holds no PHI

obligation: CIRCIA incident and ransom payment reports
citation: N92-R07: 6 U.S.C. 681-681g; proposed 6 CFR Part 226 (89 FR 23644)
trigger: Covered cyber incident or ransom payment
deadline: Proposed: 72 hours (incident); 24 hours after a ransom payment
applies_at_this_tier: NOT YET REQUIRED: no final rule in the Federal Register as of 2026-09-25. The proposed size criterion would not reach an SBA-small business

obligation: Covered telecommunications equipment or services discovered
trigger: Contractor identifies covered telecommunications equipment or services in use or delivered under a federal contract
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification (further report within 10 business days)
applies_at_this_tier: No - the owner holds no federal contracts or subcontracts

obligation: Kaspersky covered article discovered
trigger: Contractor identifies a covered article (Kaspersky Lab hardware, software, or services) in use or delivered under a federal contract
deadline: Within 3 business days of identification (further report within 10 business days)
applies_at_this_tier: No - the owner holds no federal contracts or subcontracts
